items: **Predecessor:** succeeds the PLI Scheme for Large-Scale Electronics Manufacturing, which ended on 31 March 2026.

**I-2SEA:** subsea cable project linking India with Singapore and Malaysia; described as India's first subsea cable system.
**Planned landing points in India:** Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, and South Chennai.
**Estimated cable length:** 3,600 km from Singapore to Machilipatnam, with onward connectivity to Hyderabad.
**Purpose:** intended to provide high-capacity, low-latency connectivity for AI workloads.

**GaN (Gallium Nitride):** a semiconductor material suitable for high-frequency and high-power applications.
**13 May 2026:** SAMEER and ISRO's ISTRAC agreed to develop X-band deep-space communication amplifiers using indigenous GaN chips from GAETEC/DRDO.
**Applications:** radar transmitters; electronic warfare systems; communications; intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance; unmanned systems; space and aerospace; 5G; satellite communications.
**GaN-on-SiC:** advanced high-frequency/high-power semiconductor technology; offers higher efficiency, reduces size and weight, and improves performance.
**Defence innovation:** under iDEX, a contract was signed with Agnit Semiconductors Private Limited to develop advanced GaN semiconductors for next-generation defence wireless transmitters.

parts.t: Agricultural AI: Google DeepMind's ALU and AMED models
items: **Developer:** Google DeepMind's AnthroKrishi team; the models are ALU and AMED (agricultural AI and satellite-based technology).
**ALU:** maps agricultural landscapes; identifies individual field boundaries; maps trees and woodlands; identifies small irrigation structures, including wells and dug ponds.
**ALU data:** available through APIs and as a layer in Google Earth.
AMED – Agricultural Monitoring and Event Detection
**AMED:** tracks agricultural activity at field level; identifies likely crops; estimates sowing and harvesting periods.
**Applications:** agriculture, agricultural credit, water management, policy planning and sustainable rice cultivation.
**CarbonFarm:** uses the ALU API along with Google's Gemini; automates field-level insights, including field-boundary mapping.
**CarbonFarm's aim:** intended to support programmes that reduce the environmental impact of rice farming.

parts.t: JAMA: the 49th human blood group system
items: **JAMA:** recognised by the International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT) as the 49th human blood group system; number ISBT 049.
**Discovery:** resulted from a joint investigation by researchers in the United Kingdom and Israel.
**Samples:** unusual blood samples came from an Israeli woman and her brother.
**Finding:** the woman had an antibody that reacted with the red blood cells of most people, but not her own or her brother's; researchers identified a previously unrecognised antigen.
**JAMA** is not another ABO category alongside A, B, AB and O. It is a separate blood group system involving a specific red-cell antigen; the antigen was absent in the woman and her brother.

parts.t: New research facilities: BSL-4 laboratory and high-altitude centre
items: **Foundation stone:** 13 January 2026, laid by Amit Shah.
**Status:** described as India's first state-funded Bio-Safety Level-4 (BSL-4) bio-containment facility.
**BSL-4:** the highest biosafety containment level; designed for research involving the world's most dangerous pathogens, including Ebola, Nipah and Marburg.
**Existing civilian BSL-4 laboratory:** National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune, Maharashtra; it was the only functional civilian BSL-4 laboratory in India at the time.
ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research
**Location:** Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh.
**Foundation stone:** laid on 12 October 2026 by Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda.
**Status:** first dedicated ICMR centre of this kind.

**Research areas:** effects of extreme altitude on human health; extreme weather and climate variability; geographical isolation; health of high-altitude and tribal populations; prevention and treatment of mountain-related illnesses.
**Launch:** nationwide free HPV vaccination campaign launched on 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, Rajasthan.
**Target group:** 14-year-old girls across 36 States and UTs; estimated annual beneficiaries 1.2 crore girls.
**Dose:** single dose of 0.5 ml, intramuscular injection in the left upper arm.
**Consent:** voluntary and free, with parental/guardian consent.
**Digital platforms:** U-WIN for registration and session management; e-VIN for vaccine stocks and logistics.
**TAK-003 (Qdenga):** tetravalent dengue vaccine developed by Takeda Pharma, Japan; a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine; age group 4–60 years.
**Composition:** contains weakened versions of dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, 3 and 4; uses DENV2 as the genomic backbone.
**Schedule:** two doses, three months apart, for specified groups and circumstances according to WHO recommendations.
**Approval:** CDSCO marketing authorisation in July 2026; described as India's first approved dengue vaccine.
**AdFalciVax:** Indian malaria vaccine candidate developed by Regional Medical Research Centre, Bhubaneswar, under ICMR.
**Type:** recombinant multi-stage malaria vaccine candidate; targets Plasmodium falciparum.
**Aim:** intended to prevent individual infection and reduce community-level transmission.
**Licensing:** technology licensed to five Indian companies by 17 June 2026.
**Stage:** still at preclinical stage (TRL 4) and not approved for clinical use.
Up to 12 months at normal room temperature
**WHO-recommended malaria vaccines:** RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) and R21/Matrix-M; both WHO-prequalified for widespread use in children.
**India's malaria targets:** zero indigenous malaria cases by 2027; full elimination by 2030.

parts.t: WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2025 and India's TB indicators
items: **WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2025:** released on 12 November 2025 (under World Health Statistics and TB developments); based mainly on data up to 2024.
**Coverage:** data from 184 countries and areas, covering more than 99% of the global population.
**Global TB burden in 2024:** an estimated 10.7 million people developed TB; 131 new cases per 100,000 population worldwide.
**Standing:** TB remains one of the world's leading causes of death from a single infectious agent.
**Incidence:** declined 21% from 237 per lakh population in 2015 to 187 in 2024.
**TB mortality:** declined from 28 to 21 per lakh population.
**Treatment coverage:** increased from 53% in 2015 to over 92% in 2024.
**Diagnosis:** 26.18 lakh TB patients diagnosed in India in 2024, out of an estimated 27 lakh incident cases.
**Missing cases:** reduced from 15 lakh in 2015 to less than one lakh in 2024.
KAL – India's indigenous long-range attack drone
**KAL:** autonomous one-way attack drone developed by IG Defence, Noida; trial location Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
**Role:** designed for autonomous strike missions; described as India's first indigenous long-range attack drone.
**Caution:** the specifications are manufacturer-declared, not independent operational-performance verification.
**NIDAR 2.0:** National Innovation Challenge for Drone Application and Research; launched on 13 July 2026 by MeitY and Drone Federation India; period 2026–27.
**Initiative:** second edition, launched under the SwaYaan initiative; India's largest drone innovation challenge (a national drone innovation challenge).
**Promotes student-led innovation in:** autonomous drones, indigenous avionics, navigation technology and critical drone components.
**Shift of focus:** towards autonomous systems, avionics, navigation and core components rather than conventional drone airframes.
Ahuti Mk II – electric multirotor interceptor
**Developer:** Hyderabad-based Apollyon Dynamics; associated with the BITS Pilani Hyderabad Campus startup ecosystem.
**Recorded developmental test speed:** 498 km/h; record confirmed on 29 August 2026 and published on 1 September 2026.
**Distinction:** the manufacturer distinguishes the developmental test speed from the approximately 400 km/h operational speed band targeted for production interceptors.
**Founders:** Jayant Khatri and Sourya Choudhury; early development supported through the BITS Pilani SOLVE programme.
**Full form:** Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard Kill Assets Management.
**Developer:** Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL); the Indian Army initiated procurement.
**Designed to:** detect drones; track and identify aerial threats; neutralise enemy drones and unmanned aerial systems in real time; protect border areas.
**Production version:** launched on 29 November 2025 at Bengaluru by Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh.
**Designed for:** Private Pilot Licence (PPL) training and Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) training.
**History:** the original HANSA-3 design was developed in the early 1990s; the latest version incorporates significant upgrades.
**Developer:** DRDO's Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE); industry partner Hyderabad-based Azad Engineering.
**Class:** designed in the 350 kg thrust class; successfully realised and delivered to GTRE on 22 July 2026.
**Significance:** represents an indigenous capability in expendable turbojet-engine development.
**Inaugurated:** 17 July 2026 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi; route Jind–Sonipat, Haryana; Northern Railway.
**Technology:** uses hydrogen fuel-cell propulsion; designed to generate electricity onboard using hydrogen.
**Design:** developed in India in accordance with technical specifications and design approvals prepared by RDSO.
2 hydrogen driving power cars + 8 trailer coaches
**How it works:** hydrogen reacts with oxygen in the fuel cell; the chemical reaction generates electricity; the process produces water vapour and heat as by-products.
**Driving power car:** each contains fuel cells, lithium iron phosphate batteries and hydrogen storage cylinders.
**Energy content:** hydrogen's energy content is 120 MJ/kg, compared with 43 MJ/kg for diesel.
This train is hydrogen fuel-cell powered; it is not a conventional battery-electric train.
**Flagged off:** 27 September 2026 at Sabarmati Railway Station, Ahmedabad, by Union Home Minister Amit Shah; fuel Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG).
**Train:** a Diesel Electric Multiple Unit (DEMU) converted to use LNG; two converted Driving Power Cars, each rated at 1,400 HP.
**Fuel system:** can substitute up to approximately 40% of diesel consumption with LNG; each power car has a 2,200-litre LNG tank.
**Onboard system:** includes LNG receiving, storage and regasification equipment.
**Trials and journey:** completed more than 2,000 km of field trials; inaugural journey Sabarmati to Mahesana Junction.
The 40% figure is diesel substitution, not a measured 40% reduction in emissions.
Green Hydrogen Certification Portal of India (GHCI)
**Launched:** 17 June 2026 by Union Minister Pralhad Joshi.
**Developed by:** National e-Governance Division (NeGD) for MNRE, under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
**Role:** digital operational backbone of India's Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme; provides a unified mechanism to certify green hydrogen produced in India.
**Green hydrogen:** hydrogen produced using renewable energy rather than fossil fuels.
E-methanol plant and indigenous shipping container
**India's first port-based e-methanol production plant:** foundation stone laid at Kandla, Gujarat; the project relates to the development of low-carbon fuel production infrastructure.
**India's first indigenous EXIM shipping container:** unveiled on 3 July 2026 at the Maersk–CONCOR Inland Container Depot, Dadri, Uttar Pradesh, by Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.
**Container:** made for global shipping company A.P. Moller–Maersk; supported by the ₹10,000-crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme.
**Government target:** increase annual container manufacturing capacity to approximately 7.5 lakh TEUs.
